description: Lower limit of the stepped size score: below wave_ideal_low_m the score drops in 0.1 steps and reaches 0.1 at this height; below it the score is 0 (flat). Compared with the forecast significant wave height, which is roughly 1 to 2 times the surfed face height (faces are typically 50-100% of forecast swell height per Rapture Camps)
source: Beginner 0.1 m is a DESIGN CHOICE (2026-10-17) so that beginners also get graded scores below the 1 ft ideal minimum: 1 ft (0.3 m) is about the smallest surfable size except on a longboard (https://sharpeyesurfboards.com/pages/faqs), so 0.1-0.3 m scores low but not 0; intermediate 2 ft (0.6 m) lower end of the 2-4 ft intermediate sweet spot (same source); advanced 1.0 m = lower end of the 3-5 ft intermediate range (https://climeradar.com/blog/surfing-weather-cheat-sheet)

description: Size score is 1 from this height (inside the ideal range)
source: Beginner 1-2 ft (0.3-0.6 m) is the perfect beginner size (https://sharpeyesurfboards.com/pages/faqs); intermediate 3-5 ft (1-1.5 m) and advanced 5 ft+ (1.5 m+) (https://climeradar.com/blog/surfing-weather-cheat-sheet)

description: Size score stays 1 up to this height (inside the ideal range)
source: Beginner upper end of 1-2 ft (https://sharpeyesurfboards.com/pages/faqs); intermediate upper end of 3-5 ft (https://climeradar.com/blog/surfing-weather-cheat-sheet); advanced 3.0 m is a DESIGN CHOICE (sources give no upper bound for 5 ft+ overhead surf)

description: Upper limit of the stepped size score: above wave_ideal_high_m the score drops in 0.1 steps and reaches 0.1 at this height; above it the score is 0 and the spot is unsafe for this level (safety warning)
source: Beginner 3 ft (1.0 m) upper end of the beginner range (https://climeradar.com/blog/surfing-weather-cheat-sheet); intermediate 6 ft (1.8 m) where 6-8 ft is the threshold between intermediate and advanced surf (https://node.albumsurf.com/ride-the-wave-understanding-surf-conditions-between-6-and-8-feet); advanced 4.0 m is a DESIGN CHOICE cap beyond which recreational spots are treated as big-wave conditions

description: At or below this period the period score is period_floor_fit
source: 5-8 s (Rapture Camps) or 5-9 s (Climeradar) is short-period wind swell: choppy and weak (https://www.rapturecamps.com/learn-to-surf/wave-knowledge/surf-forecast-basics; https://climeradar.com/blog/surfing-weather-cheat-sheet); stricter minimum for higher levels is a DESIGN CHOICE

description: Period score reaches 1 at this period
source: 9-12 s medium-period swell where waves start to organise (https://www.rapturecamps.com/learn-to-surf/wave-knowledge/surf-forecast-basics); 10-13 s organised and powerful (https://climeradar.com/blog/surfing-weather-cheat-sheet); 8 s for beginners because 8-9 s swell still gives fun surfable waves (https://www.foammagazine.com/wave-period/)

description: Period score for very short-period (wind) swell
source: DESIGN CHOICE: short-period wind swell is still surfable but weak and choppy (Rapture Camps); beginners in white water are least affected, so their floor is highest

description: Outside the swell window the direction score drops in 0.1 steps over this many degrees, down to direction_floor_fit
source: DESIGN CHOICE: swell refracts and wraps around headlands, so energy just outside a spot's window still arrives but weaker; 30 deg is a bit more than one 16-point compass sector (22.5 deg)

description: Lowest direction score, reached at swell_window_margin_deg outside the window and kept beyond it (never 0)
source: DESIGN CHOICE (2026-10-17): a minimum of 0.1 instead of 0, so a swell direction outside the window lowers the condition fit strongly but does not set it to 0 by itself; the forecast direction is for the offshore grid point, and swell still wraps around headlands

description: Wind at or below this speed counts as light/glassy whatever its direction
source: Beaufort force 0-1 (up to 3 knots = 5.5 km/h): Calm (glassy) to Calm (rippled) sea (https://weather.metoffice.gov.uk/guides/coast-and-sea/beaufort-scale)

description: Offshore wind up to this speed is ideal
source: Beginners: below 10 knots (18.5 km/h) beginners face little difficulty (https://skateboardershq.com/what-wind-speed-surfing/); intermediate/advanced: 5-15 knots (up to 28 km/h) offshore is the sweet spot (https://www.rapturecamps.com/learn-to-surf/wave-knowledge/tides-and-wind)

description: Offshore wind score reaches 0 at this speed (too strong to paddle into waves)
source: Beginners: 10-20 knots gives less stable waves and is harder to balance, so 20 knots = 37 km/h (https://skateboardershq.com/what-wind-speed-surfing/); intermediate/advanced: 25+ knots (46 km/h) offshore makes paddling difficult (https://www.rapturecamps.com/learn-to-surf/wave-knowledge/tides-and-wind)

description: Straight onshore wind score reaches 0 at this speed
source: Light onshore under 10 knots is manageable; 15+ knots (28 km/h) significantly degrades wave quality (https://www.rapturecamps.com/learn-to-surf/wave-knowledge/tides-and-wind). With this setting a 10-knot onshore wind scores about 0.4

description: Tide score when the tide stage is not one of the spot's ideal stages
source: DESIGN CHOICE: tide preference is spot-specific (beach breaks often best on the incoming mid tide; some reefs only at high tide, per https://www.rapturecamps.com/learn-to-surf/wave-knowledge/tides-and-wind), but a wrong tide rarely makes a spot unsurfable, so it lowers the score instead of zeroing it

description: Score when the spot profile does not list the user's skill level (0 = never recommend)
source: DESIGN CHOICE (safety): never recommend a spot whose profile excludes beginners to a beginner; intermediates and advanced surfers are penalised less

description: Importance of wave size in the product
source: DESIGN CHOICE: size, period, direction and wind are weighted equally because each can make a spot unsurfable on its own

description: Importance of swell period
source: DESIGN CHOICE: see weight_size

description: Importance of swell direction
source: DESIGN CHOICE: see weight_size

description: Importance of wind
source: DESIGN CHOICE: see weight_size

description: Importance of tide
source: DESIGN CHOICE: half weight because the tide stage comes from a coarse offshore sea-level model and tide preferences in the spot profiles are the least well sourced field

description: CF at or above this counts as surfable (the surfable / not surfable call)
source: DESIGN CHOICE: midpoint of the score scale; tune on the evaluation dev set and report the sensitivity

description: CF at or above this is called Good in explanations
source: DESIGN CHOICE: upper quarter of the score scale; affects explanation wording only

description: First daylight hour considered (local time)
source: Sunrise in Taiwan ranges from 05:02 (June) to 06:40 (January) in 2025 (Keelung and Kenting, computed with the Open-Meteo Archive API daily sunrise/sunset: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api); 06:00 is a year-round compromise

description: Hours from this one on are not considered
source: Sunset in Taiwan ranges from 17:02 (December) to 18:47 (June) in 2025 (same Open-Meteo Archive calculation); hours from 18:00 are excluded year-round
